verses.text: Then Job answered,
“Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?
lines: “Truly I know that it is so,
but how can man be just with God?

verses.text: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.
lines: If he is pleased to contend with him,
he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.

verses.text: God who is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who has hardened himself against him and prospered?
lines: God who is wise in heart, and mighty in strength:
who has hardened himself against him and prospered?

verses.text: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.
lines: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it,
when he overturns them in his anger.

verses.text: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.
lines: He shakes the earth out of its place.
Its pillars tremble.

verses.text: He commands the sun and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.
lines: He commands the sun and it doesn’t rise,
and seals up the stars.

verses.text: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.
lines: He alone stretches out the heavens,
and treads on the waves of the sea.

verses.text: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.
lines: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades,
and the rooms of the south.

verses.text: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.
lines: He does great things past finding out;
yes, marvelous things without number.

verses.text: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.
lines: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him.
He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.

verses.text: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’
lines: Behold, he snatches away.
Who can hinder him?
Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’

verses.text: “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.
lines: “God will not withdraw his anger.
The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.

verses.text: How much less will I answer him, And choose my words to argue with him?
lines: How much less will I answer him,
And choose my words to argue with him?

verses.text: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.
lines: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him.
I would make supplication to my judge.

verses.text: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.
lines: If I had called, and he had answered me,
yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.

verses.text: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.
lines: For he breaks me with a storm,
and multiplies my wounds without cause.

verses.text: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
lines: He will not allow me to catch my breath,
but fills me with bitterness.

verses.text: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’
lines: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty!
If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’

verses.text: Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me. Though I am blameless, it will prove me perverse.
lines: Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me.
Though I am blameless, it will prove me perverse.

verses.text: I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.
lines: I am blameless.
I don’t respect myself.
I despise my life.

verses.text: “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.
lines: “It is all the same.
Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.

verses.text: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.
lines: If the scourge kills suddenly,
he will mock at the trial of the innocent.

verses.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?
lines: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked.
He covers the faces of its judges.
If not he, then who is it?

verses.text: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away. They see no good.
lines: “Now my days are swifter than a runner.
They flee away. They see no good.

verses.text: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.
lines: They have passed away as the swift ships,
as the eagle that swoops on the prey.

verses.text: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;’
lines: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint,
I will put off my sad face, and cheer up;’

verses.text: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that you will not hold me innocent.
lines: I am afraid of all my sorrows,
I know that you will not hold me innocent.

verses.text: I will be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
lines: I will be condemned.
Why then do I labor in vain?

verses.text: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,
lines: If I wash myself with snow,
and cleanse my hands with lye,

verses.text: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes will abhor me.
lines: yet you will plunge me in the ditch.
My own clothes will abhor me.

verses.text: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.
lines: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him,
that we should come together in judgment.

verses.text: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.
lines: There is no umpire between us,
that might lay his hand on us both.

verses.text: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;
lines: Let him take his rod away from me.
Let his terror not make me afraid;

verses.text: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.
lines: then I would speak, and not fear him,
for I am not so in myself.
